CHALLENGE C0043 | `tmpdir` is explicitly assigned via `tempfile.mkdtemp()` BEFORE the `try` block. If `mkdtemp` fails, it raises an exception and the function never enters the `try` block or its associated `except Exception` block. `tmpdir` is never used before assignment.

CHALLENGE C0060 | `re.DOTALL` is NOT used in `line_pattern`, meaning the `.+` tokens naturally stop matching at the first newline character. The regex does not greedily consume subsequent lines; it correctly matches a single-line replacement instruction exactly as designed.

CHALLENGE C0061 | The current behavior (returning 0 issues on tool failure) is an intentional fail-open for unavailable tools. Raising `ToolNotFoundError` here would propagate up and crash `evaluate_fix` entirely since there is no `except ToolNotFoundError` handler in its execution path, violating the PoC Good Enough principle.

CHALLENGE C0023 | The original regex `r"^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?$"` is mathematically correct. Because it ends with the `$` anchor, Python's regex engine is forced to match the optional error code group if it is present at the end of the line, even though the preceding message group `(.+?)` is non-greedy.

CHALLENGE C0039 | Duplicate of C0023. The regex correctly extracts the optional error code because the `$` anchor forces the engine to test the optional group before completing the match.
